summary: A proposal to add PUSH and PULL to the File Transfer Protocol as synonyms for the confusingly named STOR and RETR commands. The author argues that store and retrieve each sound ambiguous when addressed to a server.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC argues that STOR and RETR are confusing names when addressed to a server. It proposes adding PUSH and PULL as synonyms without replacing the existing commands.

subtitle: A proposal to add clearer synonyms for FTP's STOR and RETR commands.

tldr.problem: The author argues that STOR and RETR can sound ambiguous when interpreted as commands directed to an FTP server.
tldr.mechanism: He proposes PUSH as a synonym for RETR and PULL as a synonym for STOR, while keeping the existing commands.
tldr.outcome: The RFC presents a naming proposal; it does not state whether the synonyms were adopted.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 506's status as Unknown. The RFC is a proposal about FTP command names.

sections.title: Why STOR and RETR Seem Ambiguous
sections.content: The author describes STOR as telling the server to take a file in and RETR as telling it to send a file out. He argues that the words themselves can suggest the opposite direction or be unclear when understood as commands to the server.
sections.plainLanguage: The author says STOR and RETR are not easy to interpret as server commands. Their names do not clearly show which way the file moves.

sections.title: Proposed Synonyms
sections.content: The proposal is to add PUSH and PULL as synonyms for RETR and STOR, respectively. The author also mentions GIVE and TAKE as possible alternatives and says SEND should at least be a synonym for RETR.
sections.plainLanguage: The suggested names are PUSH for RETR and PULL for STOR. The author also suggests SEND for RETR as a minimum improvement.

sections.title: Adding Names Without Replacing Them
sections.content:
The author specifically proposes synonyms rather than replacements. In his view, this would leave existing user habits and automated programs undisturbed while giving newcomers alternative command names.

The RFC does not say whether any of these synonyms were implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: Existing commands would remain available, so current users and programs could keep using them. The RFC does not report what happened to the proposal.
